claims.text: Zr is a larger atomic species than Ti.
Replacing Ti with Zr in MoNbTaTiW increases atomic-size mismatch.
The increased atomic-size mismatch caused by Ti-to-Zr substitution increases lattice distortion.
The enhanced lattice strain fields impede or otherwise modify dislocation glide.
Enhanced lattice distortion can favor reversible twinning or a localized strain-induced phase transformation.
The lattice-distortion-mediated changes in dislocation and reversible deformation behavior govern the alloy's enhanced or altered strength.
Reversible twinning or phase transformation caused by lattice distortion alters thermoelastic strain recovery and cyclic hysteresis.
The initial MoNbTaTiW alloy can be prepared as a homogeneous single-phase BCC solid solution.
The controlled comparison is between nominal MoNbTaTiW and MoNbTaZrW alloys with matched processing and microstructure.
TEM and XRD will be used to verify comparable phase distributions and microstructural characteristics before testing.
Both alloy variants will undergo identical cyclic mechanical testing at temperatures up to 1000 °C and matched strain rates.
Relative to MoNbTaTiW, the Zr-containing alloy will exhibit a different hysteresis-loop shape or area and may develop a pseudoelastic plateau.
Relative to MoNbTaTiW, the Zr-containing alloy will exhibit improved or otherwise altered yield strength.
The hypothesis applies up to 1000 °C when the alloys remain homogeneous and have minimal secondary-phase formation.
High-temperature deformation mechanisms in refractory HEAs can change substantially with temperature, including twinning at lower temperatures and dynamic recrystallization near 1000–1200 °C.
Introducing Zr may cause phase-instability, secondary precipitation, or other microstructural evolution that masks or mimics lattice-distortion effects.
Any measured differences can be attributed solely to lattice distortion if processing history, phase distribution, and other microstructural characteristics are matched.

The hypothesis is falsified if the Zr-containing alloy shows no statistically significant difference in both hysteresis behavior and yield strength relative to the baseline under identical conditions.
Observation of confounding phase changes unrelated to lattice distortion would prevent the experiment from isolating lattice distortion as the governing cause.

contradictions.description: The intervention calls MoNbTaZrW a partial substitution of Ti by Zr, but the stated modified formula contains no Ti and therefore denotes complete replacement under the nominal equiatomic interpretation.
